page: Amazon Web Services g5g.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It integrates custom AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture alongside dedicated NVIDIA acceleration. The instance provides 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz with a dedicated 1:1 core-to-thread allocation, 16 GB of system memory, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. For graphics and acceleration workloads, it pairs the ARM CPU architecture with a single NVIDIA T4G GPU delivering 16 GB of VRAM. It features no local NVMe storage, relying entirely on remote elastic block storage volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average performance in general integer and multi-core computing metrics. In multi-threaded execution, stress-ng achieves 12,132.81 and Geekbench reaches a multi-core score of 5,407.0, supported by clang compilation scoring 8,615.0 and ray tracing scoring 7,109.0. Memory bandwidth scales from 53.67 GB/s for uncached writes to 121.66 GB/s for uncached reads. However, single-threaded throughput reflects architectural constraints typical of first-generation Neoverse-N1 deployments, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and lower scores in cryptographic operations and single-threaded archive compression.

The presence of the NVIDIA T4G accelerator provides efficient offloading for graphics rendering, video encoding, and targeted machine learning inference, though large language model execution remains modest, with 7B text generation recording 6.16 tokens per second. The 2 GB per vCPU ratio makes it tightly budgeted for memory-heavy algorithms. Overall, the g5g.2xlarge offers a balanced cost-efficiency profile for organizations running ARM-native Android game streaming, graphic rendering pipelines, and computer vision inference that benefit from GPU processing without requiring high-end datacenter enterprise accelerators.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance featuring an 8-core AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 ARM64 processor paired with a single NVIDIA T4G GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Equipped with 16 GB of system memory, 2 Gbps baseline networking, and zero local storage, the instance runs on the AWS Nitro System. In benchmark testing, it delivers average multi-core CPU throughput, yielding 12,132.81 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 5,407.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Single-core performance and cryptographic operations score lower, reflecting the 2.5 GHz ARMv8 core profile. The server provides balanced qualitative cost efficiency for organizations operating ARM-native Android emulation, video streaming, computer vision, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines.
